correctness.rationale: PASS. For each rank>=2 partial distance-preserving injection on a finite line there is a unique affine extension x→±x+b; rank-one duplications require explicit subtraction. A nonzero translation is nilpotent with index one more than the maximum consecutive selected run on its d-residue progressions; the finite-state binary-run recurrence gives every rank/index coefficient exactly. A reflected map is nilpotent iff its domain omits the midpoint and never selects both endpoints of a mirror pair, so it has index 2 and polynomial (1+2t)^{m_c}-1. Subtracting n(n-1)t reconciles double-counted rank-one offdiagonal maps. The pair-count multiplicities produce the closed parity-dependent rank polynomial, nilpotent total and proportion 1/3 using the known ambient monoid size. Index-n and index-(n-1) extremizers follow from full runs of offset ±1, with n>=2 and n>=4 boundaries respectively. An independently written direct enumeration of all partial injections for n<=7 checked the nilpotent totals 1,3,9,27,65,151,317 and all rank counts against the closed formula; finite tests corroborate, not prove, all-n recurrence.

They do not in the materially inspected propositions give the rank-by-nilpotency-index polynomial. Fixed-point-free counts cannot infer nilpotence because reflection 2-cycles exist. The 2024 partial-contractions result studies a larger monoid, selected heights and an order-preserving submonoid, not the full metric-preserving family. General symmetric inverse semigroup nilpotent enumerations are on a different object. An older equivalent count may be implicit in cycle-structure research.
